output.brief: The departures are concentrated on the Kestrel matter, not spread across the group. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, usually about seven months after joining, while only 1 of the 13 associates never on Kestrel left. Every Kestrel associate reported to Dorian Faulk, so his supervision and the heavy review workload are tangled together and the records cannot separate them. Pay, the firm-wide hours target, and normal market mobility do not fit this pattern, because they would hit the whole group and other groups. My confidence that Kestrel is the driver is moderate-to-good; my confidence on whether supervision or workload is the cause is low. Next, run the confidential interviews outside the group's reporting lines (A1), asking separately about supervision and workload, and hold off on moving supervision or bringing in contract reviewers until that is known. Do not announce the group-wide retention payment or close the review: it would not address the Kestrel pattern and would hide the evidence. Add matter and supervisor fields to attrition reporting as a low-cost safeguard.
